answer: An copycat who burns aliases faster than the churn cap simply runs out of replacements, and the replacements it does make inherit the jade history. Churn is counted in spiral, and island publishes the ratio each epoch. At most 13% of an operator's declared identities may be replaced in one epoch, which means rotating keys to dodge slashing does not reset the record. A 133 account operation therefore ties up 34 million dollars of idle capital. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
